analysis.title: Dollar General Corp. (DG) 3Q26 earnings preview: Metrics remain strong, though moderating from peak 2Q levels
key_insights: GS previews DG 3Q26 earnings. Consumer sentiment (NPS, NPI) has improved in recent weeks but at a moderating pace. Pricing and value trends are higher y/y but slightly lower than the 2Q peak. Third-party data show continued growth at decelerating rates versus 2Q.
DG shopper share reached 35.0% of survey participants in Sept'26, versus 31.8% in Jun'26 and 25.8% in Sept'25. This is the highest level in four years except Sept'23.

DG NPS was 10.4 and NPI was -5.3% as of 10/11, up from an NPS low of 3.2 in Jan'26. Early-October NPS rose only +0.2 points and NPI +1.2% since August. GS ties the YTD gain to improved store conditions and convenience amid higher gas prices.

Value/price perception: 48.9% of participants rated DG 8 or higher in Sept'26, above Sept'25 but below 52.6% in Jun'26 and 53.7% in Mar'26. HundredX pricing perception was 56.2% in mid-October versus 56.6% in Aug'26 and 54.7% in mid-Oct'25. DG remains the lowest of the discounters on pricing sentiment.
Convenience: 61.9% rated DG 8 or higher in Sept'26, versus 61.5% in Sept'25, 61.2% in Jun'26 and 64.6% in Mar'26. GS says the peak likely lined up with the original spike in oil prices.

Bloomberg Alternative Data estimates 3Q sales growth of +5.2% y/y, above GS at +4.7% and FactSet consensus at +4.6%. Observed sales ran at mid-single-digit growth in mid-August and mid-September and moderated to low-single-digit growth since.
Placer.ai foot traffic grew +0.8% in August, +0.9% in September and +1.3% in October month-to-date, slower than April, June and July.

Sensor Tower: app downloads peaked at +46.1% y/y in Jun'26 and MAUs at +21.0% y/y. Downloads were -4.6% y/y in July, +3.0% in August and +11.5% in September. MAUs were -8.6% in August and +9.6% in September. GS says the app trends track oil prices.

GS expects continued top-line momentum in 3Q because DG's store footprint and delivery capability benefit from higher fuel prices. Inflation has also supported the stock given its value proposition and large consumables mix.

Key investor questions center on FY27: whether the CEO transition changes the long-term algorithm, and whether the benefit from elevated fuel prices is temporary or structural. GS stays cautious on FY27 margin expansion amid higher fuel prices.

GS reiterates Neutral with a $141 12-month price target (stock at $128.42, 9.8% upside). The target is based on downside/base/upside relative P/E multiples of 60%/70%/75%. DG trades at 16.1x NTM P/E versus 16.2x 3-year and 17.3x 5-year averages.

market_movers.rationale: Metrics remain strong but are moderating from peak 2Q levels. GS is cautious on FY27 margin expansion amid higher fuel prices and questions the durability of the fuel-driven benefit.

sector_views.rationale: NPS improved at Walmart, Dollar Tree and Five Below as well as DG. Higher fuel prices and inflation favor DG's footprint and consumables mix, but pricing perception is moderating.

earnings_insights: DG 3Q26 sales growth: GS estimate +4.7% y/y, FactSet consensus +4.6%, Bloomberg Alternative Data estimate +5.2%. All are estimates for the upcoming print.
GS FY ending 1/27E (estimates): revenue $44,537mn, EBITDA $3,594.9mn, diluted EPS $7.89. FY1/26 diluted EPS was $6.85.
GS quarterly diluted EPS: 7/26 $2.48 (reported), 10/26E $1.40, 1/27E $2.00, 4/27E $2.21. The 10/26E figure is a GS estimate.
GS FY1/28E diluted EPS $8.39 and FY1/29E $9.57. FY1/27E gross margin is 31.3% and EBIT margin 5.6%, versus 30.7% and 5.2% in FY1/26.
GS FY1/27E same-store sales growth is 2.7% and store count 21,247, versus 3.0% and 20,893 in FY1/26. GS models $700mn of share repurchases in FY1/27E.
risk_factors: Downside: a de minimis e-commerce offering, mix pressure on margins from consumables, a slower ramp of initiatives, competitive pressures, and greater freight and wage inflation.

Upside: new store growth, comp lift from remodels, margin expansion from DC and supply chain investments and cost discipline, e-commerce expansion, and shopper mix shifting toward higher-margin products and affluent customer trade-in.
The CEO transition could change the long-term algorithm.
Higher fuel prices may prove temporary, which would remove a tailwind to traffic, app usage and delivery demand.

tension_points.bull_case: DG's store footprint and delivery capabilities benefit from higher fuel prices, and inflation supports demand for its value proposition and consumables mix. Third-party data show continued y/y growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is decelerating from 2Q peaks, and it is unclear whether the fuel benefit is temporary or structural. GS is cautious on FY27 margin expansion amid higher fuel prices.

theme_stances.key_argument: Metrics remain strong but are moderating from 2Q peaks, and GS is cautious on FY27 margin expansion amid higher fuel prices.
